$comment: The words a rig may use to say how it should sound. Grouped by axis, because an axis is what makes a term mean something: saying 'mid-forward' has already said 'not scooped', and a rig claiming both has claimed nothing. Nothing compiles these into a chain yet. They are here so that a person reading a preset can say whether it came out right, and so that two rigs can be compared without parsing English.

mids.about: where the middle of the range sits

terms.mid-forward: mids pushed, the part sits in front of the mix
terms.scooped: mids pulled, the part sits under everything else

highs.about: the top, and how much of it there is

terms.dark: top rolled off, tone knob down
terms.glassy: top open and hard, closer to a bell than a growl

low-end.about: how the bottom behaves, not how much of it there is

terms.tight-low-end: the bottom stops when the note does
terms.loose-low-end: the bottom blooms and hangs on

decay.about: how long a note lasts once it is struck

terms.short-decay: notes stop, whether from the hands or the strings

drive.about: how hard the amplifier is being pushed

terms.minimal-drive: breakup only where it is played hardest
terms.grit-on-attack: the front of the note breaks up and the body does not
terms.saturated: breakup throughout, part of the voice rather than an accent

attack.about: what the front of a note sounds like

terms.audible-pick-attack: the pick is a sound of its own, not just a way in
terms.percussive: the string against the fretboard is part of the sound

terms.roomy: an audible space around the part

string-noise.about: what the hands make that is not a note

terms.audible-strings: the hands moving is part of what you hear

pickup.about: where along the string the sound is taken from

terms.bridge-forward: nasal and hard, fundamental pulled back
terms.neck-forward: round and full, harmonics pulled back

movement.about: whether the tone stays put while a note lasts

terms.envelope-swept: a filter follows the note, so the vowel changes as it decays
terms.static: the tone is the same at the end of a note as at the start
